# The Ghost Nebula and Iris Nebula

Ghostly clouds of cosmic dust drift through space 1,200 light-years away in the constellation Cepheus, glowing eerily as they reflect starlight—the brightest "specter" is the Ghost Nebula, spanning over 2 light-years across. Within these stellar nurseries, dense pockets of dust are collapsing to birth new stars, while nearby the Iris Nebula shines with an otherworldly blue hue from radiation emitted by hot young stars embedded within it.
